contributorNote: Pokot (Pökoot / Suk / Bawgott) vocabulary compiled from Ven. J. P. Farler & Rev. T. Wakefield (1882), Sir Harry H. Johnston (1902), Hon. K. R. Dundas (1910 "Notes on the Tribes Inhabiting the Baringo District", JRAI Vol. 40, pp. 56–65, 72, Plates XV–XVII — audited 100% line-by-line across 11 geographical divisions, 5 pastoral divisions, 3 Kasauria migrations, 11 Hill Suk sections, 24 orten clans & totems, Ellap/Ellat, Mt. Alongol & Kerial religion, verbatim sick prayer, and 12-month Kamei/Bengat calendar), Mervyn W. H. Beech (1911 "The Suk: Their Language and Folklore"), and Juxon Barton (1921). Expanded and cross-verified with Commercially Permissive Datasets (CLDF ASJP v20 POKOT (Crazzolara 1978 / Wichmann et al., CC-BY-4.0), SIL Bloom Pökoot CC-BY-4.0).

entries.english: Moiven / Muttia (Suk names for the prehistoric stone-kraal builders on the Uasin Gishu Plateau around Sirgoit, called Il-Mokwan by the Masai and I-Sirikwa by the Nandi) & Kaparamen Salt-Lick Raid
entries.translation: Moiven / Muttia (Il-Mokwan / I-Sirikwa — raided by the Suk at Kolowa and while taking their cattle to lick salt at Kaparamen near the Kerio River)

entries.english: The 5 Pastoral Suk Divisions (Kasauria, Kacheripko, Cheptulel, Kiplegit & Exterminated Kachenwono at Ngingyang) + Kamiriongo & Tawl in Dundas (1910, pp. 57–58)
entries.translation: Kasauria, Kacheripko, Cheptulel, Kiplegit (named after their chief), Kachenwono (formerly at Ngingyang, exterminated before 1910), Kamiriongo (from Kapukou, decimated by Karamoja & rinderpest) & Tawl (from Kawin on upper Tirkwel & Chebleng Highlands)

entries.translation: Shok (named after the short sword they manufacture) • Tirruk • Krut River (Swahili: Wehe)

entries.translation: Ellap / Ellat (benevolent rain god), Mount Alongol nether-world god (steam vents & mirages), Kerial (god of thunder) • Verbatim Sick Prayer: 'If this sickness be of the rain or of the grass or of the earth, or if it be from yourself, take it away'
